title: Multi-Vector (Late Interaction) Embedding Models with Sentence Transformers
summary: The article introduces Multi-Vector (Late Interaction) Embedding Models, a new feature in Sentence Transformers v6.0, which enhances retrieval quality by preserving token-level matching information. Unlike traditional dense embedding models that compress text into a single vector, multi-vector models retain one vector per token, enabling more precise query-document interactions via the MaxSim operator. The post explains the technical implementation, benefits (e.g., improved retrieval accuracy, support for multi-requirement queries, and visual document retrieval), trade-offs (e.g., larger index size), and practical usage (e.g., loading models, encoding queries/documents, scoring, and indexing). It also covers compatibility with existing checkpoints (PyLate, ColBERT, ColPali) and provides code examples for integration.
key_points: Multi-Vector Encoder is a new model type in Sentence Transformers v6.0 for late-interaction retrieval, supporting ColBERT-style models and visual document retrieval (e.g., ColPali).
Unlike dense embedding models (single vector per text), multi-vector models retain one vector per token, enabling token-level interactions via the MaxSim operator for improved retrieval accuracy.
MaxSim scores query-document similarity by summing the highest cosine similarities between each query token and any document token, preserving contextualized matching (e.g., synonyms, paraphrases).
Benefits include better handling of multi-requirement queries, rare entities, and out-of-domain data, but at the cost of larger index sizes (e.g., 42x more storage than dense models).
Installation requires `sentence-transformers>=6.0` and optional image dependencies for visual document retrieval. Models can be loaded directly from PyLate, ColBERT, or ColPali checkpoints.
Encoding queries and documents is asymmetric: `encode_query()` and `encode_document()` apply different prefixes, length caps, and scoring masks. Outputs are lists of 2D tensors (one per input).
Scoring uses `similarity()` (full MaxSim matrix) or `similarity_pairwise()` (matched pairs). MeanMaxSim normalizes scores to [-1, 1] for cross-model comparability.

Practical applications include semantic search (exhaustive or indexed), visual/audio/video retrieval, and interpretability via token-level alignment. Indexing tools like `fast-plaid` help manage storage costs.
Token pooling and retrieve-and-rerank strategies can reduce index size. Multi-vector models outperform dense models on long-document retrieval benchmarks (e.g., MLDR).
